subject: Midterm OKR pulse: scope trims & unblock asks
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Midterm OKR pulse: scope trims & unblock asks

Team —

I pulled a short midterm pulse together (attached) ahead of next week’s QBR. High-level takeaways and asks below. Please review and reply with owners or objections by EOD Mon so I can fold changes into the deck.

Top-line OKRs (progress & proposed adjustments):

1) Latency & Cost per Token (Platform Performance) — At 62% of target cadence.
   - Status: On track for infra improvements but model tuning is behind (model experiments delayed by infra quota).
   - Proposal: Move exploratory quantization experiments for R-range models to stretch; prioritize kernel fixes (ENG-487) for this cycle.

2) Developer Adoption (Platform APIs) — At 48% of goal.
   - Status: Docs + quickstarts shipping slightly behind (docs team constrained).
   - Proposal: Reduce scope of V1 sample apps; ship core SDK updates now, sample apps in next sprint.

3) Dedicated Sales Commitments (Revenue) — At 70% pipeline coverage.
   - Status: Negotiations with 2 mid-market deals look solid; procurement lead time is the gating risk.

Asks / unblock requests:
- Infra capacity: Need temporary GPU burst (approx 3 preemptible A100-days) to finish the model tuning experiments or we will miss the quality gate. (Owner: infra lead)
- Docs: Request a 1-week focused doc sprint; recommend pulling 0.5 FTE from Solutions Engineering to assist with examples.
- Sales/Procurement: If procurement can pre-approve an exception for one expedited purchase, it will accelerate Dedicated commitments.

Attached: QBR_Midterm_v0.9.pdf, OKR_runway_v2.xlsx.

Next steps:
- Please reply with: owner names for each ask, agreement to the proposed scope trims, and any additional risks.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Laura —

Quick read and a couple clarifying points. I agree with moving the quantization experiments to stretch if infra capacity is the limiting factor. Two questions:

- The runway spreadsheet flags ENG-487 as high-impact but medium effort; can we split the kernel fix into a two-phase delivery (fast patch + follow-up refactor) so we still get partial gains before the QBR?
- For the docs sprint, who specifically would Solutions Eng handoff to? I can free up 0.25 FTE from my team but need to know the day-to-day contact.

If you want, I can open the ticket to split ENG-487 and tag eng-leads for the quick patch.

—Naomi
Director, Product Strategy

- We can allocate ~0.2 FTE (focused engineering time) from Dedicated infra to produce a fast patch for ENG-487 this sprint. That should recover ~40% of the expected latency improvement.
